ios.desc:
Five new puzzles every morning. Thousands more whenever you like.

Dayzle is a puzzle app with more than 25 games in it — Sudoku, word search, logic and visual puzzles — and tens of thousands of practice puzzles behind them, all on your phone and all working with the signal off. Each morning brings a fresh set of five that takes about ten minutes. Play one to keep your streak, and as many more as you like.

FIVE NEW PUZZLES EVERY MORNING
A daily set of five across numbers, words and visual logic, chosen so the whole set takes about ten minutes. Everyone at your level gets the same puzzles on the same date, so you can compare notes with a friend the way you would over the morning crossword. There is a daily leaderboard if you want one — everyone appears under a friendly anonymous name unless they choose otherwise. No ads and no pop-ups inside your daily set.

THOUSANDS MORE, ANY TIME
Practice any game as much as you like, at four difficulty levels — over forty thousand bundled puzzles, so there is always another one:
• Numbers — Sudoku, Mini Sudoku, Tally, Tally Hive, Abacus, Terminus, Terminus Hive, Landmark, Span
• Words — Cipher, Word Search, Tumbler, Forage, Beacon, Witness, Loom, Amble, Amble Hive
• Visual — Crowns, Crowns Hive, Equinox, Mosaic, Mosaic Hive, Trailhead, Mirror, Lattice, Parcel, Quiver, Quiver Hive
The games share one layout and one hint button, so each new one is quick to pick up, and every game has a hands-on tutorial if you'd like one. Six of them play on hexagonal boards you will not find anywhere else. Everything works offline — the puzzles, the hints, your progress.

HINTS THAT TEACH
Every game has its own hint engine, built on that game's own solver. Ask for help on a logic puzzle and the hint looks at your board as it is now, finds the next step, names the technique and shows you the cells that prove it. Ask on a memory game and it gives you the smallest next step it can and says that is what it did. If you've made a mistake somewhere, the hint finds that first and offers to clear it. The techniques it names are ones you can use on the next puzzle.

A BRAIN SCORE, BUILT FROM PLAY
• A Brain Score worked out from the puzzles you already play
• Personal bests and trends across pattern, logic, memory, speed and focus
• A streak that needs one game a day — finish all five and the day earns a gold laurel — and every tenth day earns a streak freeze that covers a day you miss
• Scores that count mistakes and hints as well as time
